title: Final Balance, Late Balance Charges and Closing
content:
# Final Balance, Late Balance Charges and Closing

Billing office terms for Window Replacement Contracts.

## Clauses

1. The balance due on a contract is the signed contract price plus the net contract charges (change orders and fees, less price credits) minus the payments received net of refunds.
2. The net charges of the contract's installation job are collected with it, so the amount due at the end is the balance due plus those job charges. *This clause is no longer in force for a payoff of an installed contract, which is collected under the current payoff terms; it remains in force for every other collection of job charges.*
3. The remaining balance falls due on the final balance due date, the stated number of calendar days after the installation completion date, and is recorded as final balance when paid.
4. For a financed contract, the lender funding is recorded as lender funding on the funding date and any remainder is paid by the customer.
5. A late balance charge applies only while the contract status is installed.
6. A late balance charge may be assessed only when the balance remains unpaid after the final balance due date, which falls the stated number of calendar days after the installation completion date. Calendar days are counted from the day after the installation completion date, and payment on the due date itself is on time.
7. The late charge is the monthly rate times the unpaid balance for each full 30-day period after the due date, never less than the minimum charge, assessed once at the end of each such period. *This clause is no longer in force for a late balance charge on an installed contract, which is figured under the current late-charge terms.* The final balance due date itself, and the rule that no late balance charge is assessed before it, remain in force as stated in clauses 3 and 6.
8. The contract closes once it is installed and the balance due is zero; an overpayment at that point is refunded as an overpayment refund.

The stated number of days is the series final-balance due days.

## The due date, counted (hypothetical)

With 5 final-balance due days and an installation completed on a hypothetical Wednesday: day 1 is the Thursday and day 5 is the Monday, so the final balance due date is that Monday.

| Balance paid on | Timing |
|---|---|
| The Monday (the due date itself) | On time |
| The Tuesday or later | After the due date |

## When a late balance charge can be assessed

| Contract status | Balance unpaid after the due date | Late balance charge |
|---|---|---|
| Installed | Yes | May be assessed |
| Installed | No (paid on or before the due date) | Not assessed |
| Any status other than installed | — | Does not apply |

## Balance due, worked (hypothetical)

A hypothetical installed contract: signed price $20,000; change orders $1,000; fees $100; credits $600; payments received $12,000 and no refunds. Net contract charges are $500 ($1,000 plus $100, less $600), and the balance due is $8,500 ($20,000 plus $500, less $12,000).
